findings.summary: Why-provenance and provenance semirings already formalize propagation of source participation/derivation tokens. Explicit ancestry or opaque source-token retention is therefore an ordinary provenance problem unless a future mechanism demonstrates more than provenance recovery.
sources: Buneman, Khanna & Tan, Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance, ICDT 2001
Green, Karvounarakis & Tannen, Provenance Semirings, PODS 2007

findings.summary: Structural-model actual causality requires counterfactual/interventional witnesses and contingency reasoning; preemption and overdetermination show that historical ancestry or simple but-for dependence is not sufficient for actual causal responsibility.
sources: Dyrkolbotn, On Preemption and Overdetermination in Formal Theories of Causality, 2017

findings.summary: Database query-answer causality operationalizes actual cause by controlled deletion under contingency sets and ranks responsibility by minimal contingency size, giving a simple explicit interventional comparator between provenance and causal credit.
sources: Bertossi et al., Causes for query answers from databases: Datalog abduction, view-updates, and integrity constraints, IJAR 2017
Chockler & Halpern, Responsibility and Blame: A Structural-Model Approach, JAIR 2004

findings.summary: Recent 2026 counterfactual credit-assignment work isolates contribution through explicit interventions and distinguishes agent contribution from environmental stochasticity. Delayed/history-specific credit alone is therefore below the contemporary causal-credit bar.
sources: Li, Lee & Bareinboim, Counterfactual Shapley Credit Assignment, RLC 2026 / arXiv:2607.16999
Meng, Policy-Conditioned Counterfactual Credit for Verifiable Reinforcement Learning of Long-Horizon Language Agents, arXiv:2606.05263
